question: Articles 36 to 51 of the Indian Constitution deal with ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive principles of State policy**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Articles 36 to 51** of the Indian Constitution deal with **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP**), which guide the State in making laws & policies
 
• These principles **aim to create a social order** characterized by justice, liberty, equality, & fraternity as outlined in the Constitution's Preamble
 
• They are **non-justiciable, **meaning they are not enforceable by courts for their violation
 
• Part IV of the Indian Constitution deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy
 
• They are **borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland**, which had copied it from the Spanish Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental rights**

 
 
• **​**Articles **12 to 35 contained in Part III** of the Constitution deal with Fundamental Rights.
 
• These are the Right to equality, including equality before the law, prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth, and equality of opportunity in matters of employment.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental duties**
 
 
• **FD which is also called ​**(Article 51A) outlines the moral obligations of citizens.
 
• Indian Fundamental Duties include abiding by the Indian Constitution, respecting our flag, keeping a sense of respect for the national anthem and protecting public property. In this constitution, through the 42nd Amendment Act 1976, the fundamental duties of citizens were listed.
 
 
 
• **Preamble of Indian constitution**
 
 
• Serves as the **introduction to the Constitution**, setting forth its ideals & goals.**​**
 
• It outlines the **sources of authority **for the Constitution and sets the tone for the entire legal framework
